subject: [PATCH] mm, swap: revalidate populated clusters before scanning

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the swap_cluster_alloc_table() function does not hold nor acquire cluster's lock, agreed to restructure in v2 to address this issue.
reviews.raw_body:
Ah nope, I saw that Kemeng implemented your approach:

https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/20260907091356.53026-2-shikemeng@huaweicloud.com/

My bad! But yeah I think we still need this small fix (or Kemeng's
original proposal?), unless I missed something...?

2026-10-20.patch_summary: This patch revalidates populated clusters before scanning to prevent potential issues where someone can free the table between publishing and lock acquisition in swap_cluster_populate(). The patch adds a simple check to cover edge cases, but it's suggested that more robust solutions could be explored by enforcing metadata lifetime or using reference counting.

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the swapoff path needs to drop the per-vswap spinlock before calling try_to_unmap(), but couldn't reproduce the issue and will report back if they manage to do so.
reviews.raw_body:
I'm revisiting the lifecycle of clusters, because vswap introduced
dynamic (i.e run-time freeing) behavior to it. For the most part it
looks good (both physical and virtual side), but this look racy to me.
I don't see how it can be safe. Once you drop the lock, all bets are
off...

But at the same time, I have not been able to reproduce it (yet). Will
report here if I manage to.

(Side note: my vswap code is actually safe in this scenario. CPU0
allocates a new cluster entirely, and lock it before publishing it. So
even if the cluster index is cached in CPU1, this race cannot happen).

2026-10-19.patch_summary: This patch revalidates populated clusters before scanning to prevent dereferencing a NULL table. It checks if the cluster's table is allocated and relocates it only when its table is present. This fix addresses an issue where a cached allocator can use and empty a cluster's table before the populating allocator reacquires the lock, leading to a NULL pointer dereference during scanning.

reviews.author: Kairui Song
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that swap_cluster_alloc_table() does not hold nor acquire the cluster's lock, allowing someone to free the table between publishing and subsequent lock acquisition in its caller, swap_cluster_populate().
